judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is a 'Saiba Mais' related-article link. Its category label 'POLÍTICA' is a strong element at 9.6 px, bold and uppercase, and inherits the link colour. I checked live: the rule '.read-more ul li a:hover { color: #00cc99 }' turns the label from #0077b6 (about 4.9:1) to #00cc99 on the white card, which is 2.08:1 (I recomputed it). It is small text, so it needs 4.5:1. The 1.4.3 Understanding says text shown while hovered must also have sufficient contrast. I found no exemption: the label is not incidental or a logo, and nothing changes behind it on hover. The title span stays #333 and passes, so the failure is the label, which is what the evidence measures.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the title span of a 'Saiba Mais' card ('Quando os resultados da eleição serão anunciados e como acompanhá-los?'). I reproduced it live at 1280x1024: the cards sit in div.slick-slider, which has a fixed height of 280px and overflow hidden. The span has line-height 16px (1.0). With the WCAG 1.4.12 spacing values, the title grows from 3 lines (49 px) to 4 lines (97 px), and the slider clips the bottom line. In the screenshot the last words, 'acompanhá-los?', disappear. The text was whole before the change. This is loss of content under the spacing values the criterion requires, and nothing in the page lets the user see the clipped line. I found no artefact.

The covering element is div.publicidade-ancorads, the site's sticky anchor-ad footer (position fixed, z-index 9999, opaque white background, 1280x110 at the bottom of the 800 px viewport; checked live). Its close control is a plain div, so a keyboard user cannot dismiss it. I checked live that the element itself keeps the browser's default focus ring (outline auto, :focus-visible matches), and that the ring shows when the element is not covered. So the indicator exists but is fully hidden. That overlaps the 2.4.11 finding for the same Tab step. Still, the 2.4.11 Understanding says that 'if the focus indicator is fully obscured, it would likely fail 2.4.7 Focus Visible'. The probe measured 0 px of change in the whole viewport, so the indicator was entirely invisible. The claim of no visible indicator, read fairly, still names a 2.4.7 failure.
